_source.title: Wikipedia: List of fake news websites (curated, every row cites sources)
Wikipedia: List of miscellaneous fake news websites
DFRLab: Russia's so-called 'Pravda' network expands worldwide (24 Feb 2025)

_notes: Inclusion rule: (a) a fact-checker, research lab, court/police action or government advisory explicitly documents REPEATED false content from the source, and for single domestic outlets also (b) the source appears on a curated, cited research list (Wikipedia fake-news-site lists). Use ONLY as provenance CONTEXT (Appearance.context_flags='known_disinfo'): 'the earliest appearance is on a source with a documented record of misinformation'. It must never by itself turn a claim FALSE, and never lower confidence in a claim that independent sources corroborate. Deliberately excluded: 'IndiaTimes.com' (appears on Wikipedia's misc list 'per PolitiFact' but indiatimes.com is the Times Group's legitimate domain - an example of why lists must not be imported blindly); mainstream outlets named in Alt News' 2022 tally (Times Group, Zee, India Today Group, NDTV) - repeat errors are not the same as being a disinformation source; indiavsdisinformation.com (on the Wikipedia list but the row only states ownership, no documented false content); worldnewsdailyreport.com (now redirects to an unrelated site); individual Meta CIB / X takedown accounts (no stable domains to match); Indian Chronicles domains (report page does not enumerate them). Handles in the Army-flagged entry are a single, government-attributed incident.

sources.name: Postcard News
sources.evidence_note: Alt News (6 Jul 2018): 'Postcard News, synonymous with misinformation in the garb of news, continues to post ... content which is communal in nature, provocative in tone and mostly untrue'. Alt News + The News Minute: founder Mahesh Vikram Hegde arrested by Karnataka police (March 2018) over a fake story about a Jain monk. Wikipedia list: 'In 2019, its founder ... was arrested for a second time on charges of spreading fake news.'
sources.site_check: postcard.news did not resolve in DNS on 2026-10-31 (keep for archived links/screenshots)
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text

sources.name: OpIndia
sources.evidence_note: Wikipedia: 'In 2019, the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) rejected OpIndia's application'; 'IFCN-certified fact checkers identified 25 fake news stories and 14 misreported stories published by OpIndia' (Jan 2018-Jun 2020). Alt News 2022 roundup: OpIndia 'was seen sharing misinformation on 18 counts this year'. Listed on Wikipedia's 'List of fake news websites'. CAUTION: the same Alt News analysis also counted misinformation by mainstream groups (Times Group 45, Zee 32, India Today 23, NDTV 14) - those are NOT listed here because they are not on curated fake-news-site lists; repeat errors alone do not make an outlet a disinfo source.
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text

sources.evidence_note: Wikipedia misc. fake news list: 'Spread COVID-19 vaccine misinformation'. PolitiFact (28 Jan 2020) on GreatGameIndia's coronavirus 'bioweapon' story: 'The story lacks evidence for its headline, so we rate it False.'
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text

sources.name: 'Indian Chronicles' influence operation (Srivastava Group network)
sources.evidence_note: EU DisinfoLab (9 Dec 2020): a 15-year operation 'led by the Srivastava Group and amplified by ANI' with '750+ fake media outlets, covering 119 countries; 550+ domain names registered'; fake EU magazines such as 'EP Today' and 'EU Chronicle'; 'Times of Geneva' and '4 News Agency' stopped activities after the 2019 investigation. The report page does not list the domains in machine-readable form, so no domains are included - match on outlet names only. NOTE: the report says ANI amplified this content; ANI itself is NOT listed as a disinfo source (it is a major wire - see syndication.json).
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text

sources.name: Accounts named by the Indian Army fact-check account (28 Oct 2026 campaign)
sources.country: PK (as attributed by the Indian Army)
sources.evidence_note: Both articles (identical copy - treat as ONE source) quote the Indian Army's fact-check post on X: it 'identified 10 social media handles allegedly involved in circulating the content between 0040 hours and 0800 hours on October 28, 2026' (a misleading video/overlay targeting the Army Chief). SINGLE government attribution for a single campaign: use only as weak context (e.g. 'this handle was named in a government advisory'), never as a verdict on an account. Handles with personal-looking names may be impersonation or misattribution.
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text

sources.name: 'Pravda' network (formerly Portal Kombat)
sources.evidence_note: Wikipedia: network of 'at least 224 sites, according to Viginum' (France); 'In 2024, many of its domains became centralized using versions of the news-pravda.com domain'; content used to influence LLM training data. DFRLab (24 Feb 2025): the network 'formerly known as Portal Kombat' expanded its infrastructure; uses 'pravda-' country-coded domains and subdomains such as usa./eu./nato.news-pravda.com. Match news-pravda.com incl. ALL subdomains, and treat 'pravda-<cc>.com' domains as candidates for manual review.
sources.verification_method: each evidence_url fetched on 2026-10-31 (HTTP 200) and the quoted wording confirmed in the page text
